scenes.narration: Across the Middle East, millions of people get their water by truck. And every one of those deliveries is paid for on the word of the person being paid.
scenes.on_screen: A water delivery is paid for on the word of the person being paid.

scenes.narration: A tanker arrives, someone signs a form, and the money moves. Nobody measured the water. In Jordan alone that is a hundred and seventy-six million dollars a year, settled on paper.

stats.cap: a year in Jordan alone, settled on paper

scenes.narration: Saqqa puts a level sensor on the buyer's tank and uses the SIM already in the tanker's cab. Then it asks the mobile operator to be the witness, and pays only for the litres it can account for.
steps: A level sensor on the buyer's tank
The SIM already in the tanker's cab
The mobile operator is the witness

scenes.narration: Here is an honest delivery. One click, and the agent makes about ten live calls to the network: where the truck was, when it reached the tank, whether the SIM is the one we expect. The tank rose while the truck was there. Two clocks agree. Payment released.

Now the one that matters. The tank rises at five past nine. The operator's timestamps put the truck at the tank at twenty-five to ten. The network contradicts our own sensor, and the agent refuses to believe its own sensor. Nothing is paid until a person looks.
scenes.on_screen: The agent doubts its own sensor

scenes.narration: Switch to the core profile, the three APIs Saqqa needs at minimum. A perfect delivery, but the number the money would go to changed SIM nineteen hours ago. Blocked, before a dinar moves. And the agent names every check it could not run.
scenes.on_screen: Blocked on three APIs, before a dinar moves

scenes.narration: Seven CAMARA APIs across two categories, orchestrated by one LangGraph agent, live on Nokia Network as Code. A hundred and twenty-five live calls in testing. Zero errors.
scenes.on_screen: 7 CAMARA APIs · 1 agent · 125 live calls · 0 errors

scenes.narration: A truckload is worth about thirty dollars. Verifying it costs thirteen cents. Nothing to install on the truck, one sensor on the tank, and the delivery form the buyer already uses, filled in from evidence instead of a signature.
scenes.on_screen: Cheap to verify. Nothing to install.
